key_insight: The aerofoil leading edge does not simply passively “image” upstream turbulence: after a short linear-distortion region, local generation and pressure–strain effects create new turbulence near the nose.
engineering_relevance: For leading-edge noise prediction, models that include this breakdown of rapid-distortion linearity can improve Amiet-based acoustic estimates and transfer across different nose radii.
method: Computed grid turbulence over a NACA 0012 aerofoil.
Sampled turbulence on three congruent surfaces around the leading edge and formed cross-spectral tensors between upstream and pre-impact stations.
Compared results with a no-aerofoil control and interpreted anisotropy changes using pressure–strain and rapid-distortion theory.
evidence_signal: The linearity spectrum drops by about 3× at energy-containing scales (k r_LE ≈ 0.3), and the anisotropy invariant changes sign near x ≈ -1.5 r_LE across a 14× range in nose radius.
watch_item: The mapping is improved but still model-dependent: it is validated against a specific aerofoil/control setup and may require careful recalibration outside the tested nose-radius and inflow conditions.
paper_title: Turbulence at an aerofoil leading edge: the linearity boundary and its generation mechanism
